Key Points
• Homocysteine is a sulfur amino acid and product of methionine metabolism.
• Homocysteine metabolism requires several B-vitamins, including folate, B12, B6, and riboﬂavin.
• Hyperhomocysteinemia is caused by B vitamin deﬁciencies, genetic defects, and other pathophysiological conditions,
including renal disease and hypothyroidism.
• Hyperhomocysteinemia is a risk factor for vascular disease, and neurodegenerative disease.
• B-vitamin supplementation lowers blood homocysteine concentrations.
• It is unclear if B-vitamin supplementation reduces the risk of vascular disease and neurodegenerative disease.
